newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Honko market debut disappointing - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Honko market debut disappointing - brokers.

text.p: Transistor maker and distributor Honko International Holdings Ltd had a disappointing market debut on Monday, with its shares closing at HK$1.04 compared with an issue price of HK$1.00 per share, brokers said.
Honko shares opened at HK$1.23 and hit a session low of HK$1.03. Volume was 42.46 million shares.
"It was disappointing," said Edwin Cheung, a sales manager at Taiwan Securities. "We initially expected the shares to trade above HK$1.10 but it ended up another way round."
Honko's flotation was about 34.3 times subscribed.
"The current price was almost the cost of the shares," said Michael Ng, senior analyst at ASG Investment.
"I think the shares can edge up further as investors are not actively selling the shares on the debut."

But one research manager at a local brokerage said the company's fundamentals were not exciting. "Unexciting fundamentals, such as its business nature, are expected to keep longer-term investors away," he said.

Honko offered a total of 67 million shares at HK$1.00 each with warrants in the proportion of one warrant 0640.HK for every five shares subscribed. It said proceeds would be used to fund the expansion of production facilities.
